- Chirp already owns the right patch point: **`/Users/pablofernandez/Work/chirp/apps/ios/scripts/regen-flatbuffers.sh`** — created (chirp#35) precisely because these files used to be hand-run flatc. Add a post-process step there. [...] 1. A small idempotent script (e.g. `apps/ios/scripts/neuter-slow-flatbuffer-accessors.sh`, sed/python): for every `public var <name>: FlatbufferVector<UInt8>` with a sibling `withUnsafePointerTo<Name>` in `apps/ios/Chirp/Bridge/Generated/*.generated.swift`, prepend the `@available(*, unavailable, ...)` line. Run it once now over checked-in files; call it from `regen-flatbuffers.sh` after each flatc invocation.
2. A CI presence check in `.github/workflows/codegen-drift.yml`: fail if any `FlatbufferVector<UInt8>` accessor lacks the annotation — catches future hand-run flatc regens.
3. First migrate the one in-tree consumer of a slow accessor besides your fix, if any (I found only `KernelUpdateFrameDecoder.swift` and `TypedHomeFeedDecoder.swift` touch these; the latter already uses the fast path). [...] - **The right patch point already exists:** `apps/ios/scripts/regen-flatbuffers.sh` in the chirp repo (created for chirp#35). Verified it's safe to neuter the slow accessor — it's referenced nowhere else in the generated file (verifier/builders go through `VTOFFSET` directly) — so marking it `@available(*, unavailable, message: "...")` turns any future misuse into a compile error, with a minimal diff against fresh flatc output. [...] User: implement the @available annotation fix now [...] **The `@available` neutering (as planned):**
- New `apps/ios/scripts/neuter-slow-flatbuffer-accessors.sh` in chirp — idempotent, finds every `FlatbufferVector<UInt8>` accessor with a fast sibling and marks it `@available(*, unavailable, ...)`. Verified idempotent (reruns annotate 0).
- Wired into `regen-flatbuffers.sh` so it runs after every future flatc regen.
- New `ci/check-flatbuffer-byte-vector-accessors.sh` + a `flatbuffer-byte-vector-accessors` job in `codegen-drift.yml` — verified it actually fails when an annotation is stripped, and passes when restored.
- Applied once now: 8 accessors annotated across 5 files.
